sources.title: Kabir et al. 2020, A deep convolutional neural network model for rapid prediction of fluvial flood inundation
sources.verified: 5m EA LiDAR further processed by Bristol, including removal of trees and bridges; 2005 flow inputs routed with 1D model, not direct measurement at inlet; time zero Jan7 00:00. Does not identify buildings at the81 suspect point cells.
sources.claim_limit: CNN targets are LISFLOOD outputs; cannot transfer reported software agreement to real-world accuracy.

sources.title: McClean et al. 2020, Implications of Using Global Digital Elevation Models for Flood Risk Analysis in Cities
sources.verified: 263 observations are elevations above sea level; paper retains points below DEM in numerical diagnostics. Building/bridge treatment is feature-dependent; this paper does not resolve our specific81 cells.
sources.claim_limit: No permission to convert Z minus uncertain terrain into exact measured depth, remove high cells, or replace5m with50m.

sources.title: Neal et al. 2009 original observation study
sources.verified: DOI10.1016/j.jhydrol.2009.01.026 and publication identity only; full original text not obtained in this unit.

sources.title: Parkes et al. 2013, Reducing Inconsistencies in Point Observations of Maximum Flood Inundation Level
sources.verified: publisher full page returned403; no alternate-entry retry; search snippet not sufficient to assign point-specific uncertainty
sources.claim_limit: Do not add0.51m uniformly, shift observed elevations, or adopt snippet uncertainty as a new acceptance tolerance.

why: These are archived samples from distinct terrain representations, not a new consistent regridding of one verified raw ground surface. Only point attributes available here.
next_discriminating_work: After complete result, cross-tab all known misses with elevation flags without exclusion. Obtain matching raw terrain/building-processing provenance before any geometry edit; absent provenance, mark attribution unresolved and retain original input.
